text: I am separating two targets: Q\(\)s strategic equilibrium claim for peer scoring and P\(\)s statistical target identification under a common flip. I will test whether Q\(\)s scoring assumptions survive P\(\)s observational ambiguity, then look for a concrete repair or impossibility.

Initial source check: the supplied P.tex is itself a manuscript about a different internal Q (learning-augmented algorithms) and internal P (peer-derived Bradley--Terry rankings); its internal labels are not this pair. For the actual pair, Q.tex lines 1651-1734 proves peer discipline from known, distinct type-conditioned co-player beliefs \(\beta_i[t_i]\) with scoring gap \(\Lambda\|\beta_i[t_i]-\beta_i[\hat t_i]\|_2^2\). P.tex lines 63-96 proves that shared item flips can preserve the entire peer-report law while reversing an intended endpoint score order on a path. The apparent bridge is the difference between incentive compatibility for a known predictive type map and statistical certification that the reports target the intended latent object. I am testing a precise formulation rather than transferring either theorem wholesale.

Q.tex 1651-1734 assumes a known map \(t_i\mapsto\beta_i[t_i]\) and separation \(\beta_i[t_i]\ne\beta_i[\hat t_i]\); its quadratic score gives the exact truthful-report margin \(\Lambda\|\beta_i[t_i]-\beta_i[\hat t_i]\|_2^2\), then cancels reported utility and prohibits off-support actions. Q.tex 1436-1506 explicitly permits correlated interim signals and puts state beliefs inside universal types. Thus independence is not needed for Q strategic IC, but the peer score only verifies the reported forecast of other reports. P.tex 63-96 has an equal-full-report-law clean/common-flip pair with opposite endpoint target order, so report agreement alone cannot identify that target. I am constructing a minimal Q-style binary example in which strict peer-belief separation holds although the peer signals can be entirely independent of the human target.

I will pursue a direct composition that P does not state: put Q-style quadratic peer scoring on each observer\(\)s private vector of labels on P\(\)s four-vertex path. For any positive observer reliabilities, the co-player conditional laws separate distinct label vectors, so truthful reporting can be strict in both of P\(\)s observationally identical worlds, yet the endpoint order remains opposite. I will also state exactly which extra information repairs identification (restricted constant flip rate from a nondegenerate short cycle, a known flip rate, or external target anchors), without claiming Q\(\)s full state-dependent mechanism is refuted.

A separate contractibility caveat in Q: Q.tex 1647 says co-player scoring applies when ground truth is unavailable, but its general schedule (PR), Q.tex 1680-1734, is \(r_i(\hat t,a,\theta)\); both the cancellation \(-u_i[\hat t_i](a,\theta)\) and the \(-\infty\) support test can depend on the true state \(\theta\). Q.tex 917-948 itself distinguishes no-state-measure mechanisms from full contractability. Therefore the general any-feasible-rule proposition is conditional on state-contingent reward access; the binary worked example at 1737-1780 is a special case where rewards depend only on reports and actions. This is an application boundary, not an internal contradiction. P.tex 63-96 makes a peer-only replacement for the missing state measure questionable because the full report law can conceal target reversal.

Possible quantitative bridge beyond the exact examples: Q\(\)s score is \(S(q,y)=2q_y-\|q\|_2^2\). If the designer uses calibrated conditional peer laws \(q_t\) but a true type \(t\) predicts \(p_t\) with \(\|p_t-q_t\|_2\le\epsilon\), then its expected truthful-minus-false score against \(s\) equals \(\|q_t-q_s\|_2^2+2(p_t-q_t)\cdot(q_t-q_s)\ge d_{ts}(d_{ts}-2\epsilon)\), where \(d_{ts}=\|q_t-q_s\|_2\). Replacing Q\(\)s exact separation gap by \(m=\min_{t\ne s}d_{ts}(d_{ts}-2\epsilon)>0\), \(\Lambda m>M\) preserves Q\(\)s truth-telling argument (assuming the same finite action/type and enforceable support conditions). This addresses strategic robustness only. P\(\)s identical-report-law worlds have identical \(p_t\), even \(\epsilon=0\), yet opposite endpoint targets, so no choice of \(\Lambda\) repairs statistical identification.

Independent minimal witness (simpler than P path, but P supplies the structured rank reversal): let \(C\) be uniform on \(\{-1,+1\}\), \(Z_1,Z_2\) independent with \(\mathbb E Z_i=a\in(0,1)\), and observable private labels \(T_i=CZ_i\). Then \(\Pr(T_2=y\mid T_1=x)=(1+a^2xy)/2\), so the two conditional peer laws have squared separation \(2a^4>0\), and Q\(\)s peer score strictly rewards truthful label reports. World A sets human target \(\theta=C\); world B takes \(\theta\) independent uniform. The complete observable label law and every peer-score incentive are identical, but choosing \(A=T_1\) has target accuracy \((1+a)/2\) in A and \(1/2\) in B. This shows separated peer beliefs can come wholly from a task-irrelevant common shock. Caveat: Q\(\)s full universal types include beliefs about \(\theta\), so the full theoretical types differ between worlds; the indistinguishability claim concerns what a designer can learn from peer labels without the state-belief map, not a contradiction of Q given known \(\Gamma\). Q.tex 1465-1493 and 1651-1695; P.tex 63-96.

Concrete composition proved in ada/truthful_peer_scores_hidden_target.md: two observers privately receive full three-edge label vectors on P\(\)s four-vertex path, with independent positive personal reliabilities. For each edge, \(w_e=\mathbb E(X_eB_e)\), and \(\mathbb E[Y_{ej}\mid Y_{ei}=+1]-\mathbb E[Y_{ej}\mid Y_{ei}=-1]=2a_ia_j(1-w_e^2)/(1-a_i^2w_e^2)>0\). Thus distinct label-vector types have distinct co-player conditional laws, satisfying Q\(\)s strict separation. The joint label law, hence Q\(\)s quadratic-score table and truthful-report incentive margin, is identical in P\(\)s clean and shared-flip worlds, while their intended endpoint differences are \(1\) and approximately \(-0.26458\). Therefore strict truthful peer reporting and complete agreement-law identification coexist with a minimax endpoint-order error of at least \(1/2\). This is a specialization to label-as-type, singleton action, and truthful equilibrium; it does not refute Q\(\)s full proposition.

Concrete audit for the P counterexample: its path differences are \((4,-3/2,-3/2)\) with common rate \(b=1/2\) (P.tex 74-96). Adding a comparison edge \((1,3)\) gives a nondegenerate triangle with differences \(4,-3/2,5/2\); the calibrated means \(A=w_{12},B=w_{23},C=w_{13}\) identify \(b^2=ABC/(A+B-C)\) by P.tex 112-126. Thus this single new edge, under P\(\)s edge-homogeneous flip restriction, removes the path ambiguity in the population, while collecting arbitrarily many new peer labels on only the old path does not. This is a statistical repair; Q still needs correctly specified co-player belief forecasts and enforceable utility/action rewards for strategic implementation (Q.tex 1651-1734). External target anchors or a known \(b\) are other repairs; unrestricted correlated noise is not covered.

Cross-check of ada/\(\)s composition: the conditional-mean difference in entry 8 follows from \(\mathbb E Y_i=a_iw\), \(\mathbb E Y_j=a_jw\), \(\mathbb E Y_iY_j=a_ia_j\); it is strictly positive when \(a_i,a_j>0\) and \(|w|<1\). Independent edge draws make label-vector predictive laws injective as claimed. The intended endpoint signs match P.tex 86-94. Important ontology boundary: Q.tex 1450-1470 defines a full type with beliefs about \(\theta\), so the label-vector types in the two worlds need not be the same full universal types; the result is an operational label-report specialization with the same score table, not a contradiction to Q under a known state/type law.

Prior-work check (queries: "peer prediction correlated signals common noise uninformative truthfulness ground truth paper"; "peer prediction mechanism truthful reports uninformative common signal target accuracy impossibility paper"; "peer prediction correlated error latent common shock information state identification scoring rules"). Miller, Resnick, Zeckhauser 2005 explicitly score a signal through another rater\(\)s report and prove honest reporting as an equilibrium (https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.1050.0379). Shnayder et al. 2016 distinguish truthful equilibria from uninformative ones and study stronger informed-truthfulness criteria (https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.03151). Hence the generic distinction between truthful peer reports and target truth is established background, not a novelty claim. The distinctive candidate here is P\(\)s structured Bradley--Terry rank reversal coexisting with Q\(\)s strict score separation, plus an explicit graph audit. I have not established that this exact composition is absent from prior work.

Boundary on the composition: Q.tex lines 1680-1697 permits state-dependent reward terms, including cancellation of reported utility and an off-support test; Q.tex lines 1702-1734 uses these to implement arbitrary feasible actions. My constructed game sets utilities to zero and the action set to a singleton, so the same report-only quadratic score works in both P worlds. This proves that strategic truthfulness of peer labels does not identify P\(\)s intended ranking; it does not show that Q\(\)s full state-contingent implementation fails. For a statistical repair under P.tex lines 118-134, the cycle formula requires calibrated edge means, hence known reliabilities or P\(\)s three-observer overlap calibration (P.tex lines 46-60), plus an edge-constant positive common-flip model.

Sharpened question for a possible paper: in a peer-score game with strictly truthful label reports, when is the intended Bradley--Terry ranking a function of the equilibrium report law, and what comparison-graph audit breaks observational aliases? Q.tex 1651-1734 supplies the strategic score margin; P.tex 63-96 supplies a same-law/opposite-rank path, and P.tex 112-134 supplies a conditional short-cycle repair. Ada\(\)s entry 8 proves the direct composition; my entries 9-11 add one-edge audit, contractibility and prior-work boundaries, and a robust score-margin calculation. This is a supported research direction, not a present novelty claim. Unresolved: general noise classes, minimal audit graph beyond this path, finite-sample calibration and strategic equilibrium selection, and whether any stronger result survives unrestricted correlated noise.
ready at #13

Cross-checked emmy\(\)s prior-work boundary against primary pages: Miller, Resnick, and Zeckhauser (2005) explicitly state that scoring implied predictions of another rater\(\)s report makes truthful signal reporting a Nash equilibrium (https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.1050.0379). Shnayder et al. (2016) explicitly study uninformative equilibria and informed truthfulness (https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.03151). Thus the broad truthful-peer-report-versus-target distinction is prior background; the narrower Q/P contribution would need the structured rank-reversal and audit result, plus a further general or finite-sample advance for a strong publication claim. Search queries run: "Miller Resnick Zeckhauser 2005 eliciting informative feedback peer prediction honest reporting equilibrium pdf"; "Shnayder Agarwal Frongillo Parkes informed truthfulness peer prediction uninformative equilibria 2016 pdf".

Sharpened question and assessment: for a peer-only mechanism with strict truthful reporting of observed labels, when is an intended Bradley--Terry ranking a function of the equilibrium report law? Q.tex lines 1651-1734 alone answers the incentive question conditional on known peer-belief maps; P.tex lines 63-96 answers the report-law ambiguity on a path. Their composition in ada/truthful_peer_scores_hidden_target.md gives a strict truthful equilibrium in both indistinguishable worlds, so no report-only score scaling fixes the target ambiguity. Under P\(\)s restricted constant positive common-flip model, a known rate or nondegenerate short cycle plus calibrated observer reliabilities repairs population identification (P.tex lines 46-60, 118-134); emmy\(\)s one-edge audit at #9 is a concrete path repair. This composition is a supported direction but likely too incremental for a paper by itself; unresolved are general noise classes, minimal audits, finite-sample stability, and equilibrium selection. The note passed style-ban-artifacts and style_gate.py with zero errors or warnings.
ready at #16

A new audit-limit counterexample: add edge \(1\to3\) to P.tex 74-96 path, so the comparison graph has a triangle and a tail. World A has differences \(d_{12}=4,d_{23}=d_{34}=-3/2,d_{13}=5/2\) and constant common-flip mean \(b_e=1/2\), hence \(c_1-c_4=1\). World B has \(d'_{12}=13/5,d'_{23}=d'_{34}=-3/2,d'_{13}=11/10\), hence \(c'_1-c'_4=-2/5\). Choose edge-specific positive means \(b'_e=w_e/\tanh(d'_e/2)\), where \(w_e=(1/2)\tanh(d_e/2)\). In edge order \(12,23,34,13\), these are approximately \((0.55936,0.5,0.5,0.84740)\), all in \((0,1)\). Independent edge draws, independent common flips and the same positive-reliability peer channels give exactly the same full peer-report law in A and B, since each shared latent edge sign has the same mean \(w_e\). The Q quadratic score table and strict separation are therefore identical in both. The triangle formula in P.tex 118-134 returns \(b=1/2\) from this law but cannot verify that the true world has constant \(b\). Thus the one-edge audit from my #9 repairs target identification only under an externally justified edge-homogeneity restriction; a report-only goodness-of-fit check cannot certify it.

Entry #18 suggests an exact heterogeneous-noise boundary beyond the triangle example. Assume independent items, calibrated positive observer reliabilities, and independent edge-specific common flips with unknown means \(b_e\in(0,1]\), so \(w_e=b_e\tanh((c_u-c_v)/2)\). For nonzero \(w_e\), orient each comparison edge from larger to smaller score according to \(\operatorname{sgn}w_e\). If this orientation is feasible, then a pairwise order is identified from the full peer-report law exactly when one vertex reaches the other in this directed graph. Reachability forces the order. For incomparable vertices, choose either linear extension, assign descending scores with spacing larger than every \(2\operatorname{artanh}|w_e|\), and set \(b_e=w_e/\tanh((c_u-c_v)/2)\in(0,1)\). Both worlds have the same latent corrupted-sign means, and hence the same complete peer-report law under the independent channel, while reversing the pair. Q-style strict score separation still holds by the calculation in #8. This is a proposed generalization; I will formalize and check boundaries before ready.

Generalization of #18 within the edge-specific positive common-flip class: a connected comparison graph universally identifies every pairwise Bradley--Terry order from population peer-report laws if and only if it is complete (assuming known or calibratable positive observer reliabilities and independent edge draws). Sufficiency: each pair has a direct edge and \(w_{uv}=b_{uv}\tanh((c_u-c_v)/2)\) with \(b_{uv}>0\), so \(\operatorname{sgn}w_{uv}=\operatorname{sgn}(c_u-c_v)\). Necessity: for any missing edge \(uv\), choose two score vectors that swap \(c_u=1,c_v=0\) and \(c_u=0,c_v=1\), while every other vertex has a distinct negative score. Every observed edge has the same nonzero sign in both worlds. For each edge choose a small \(w_e\) of that sign with \(|w_e|<\min_W|\tanh(d_e^W/2)|\); set \(b_e^W=w_e/\tanh(d_e^W/2)\in(0,1)\). Then all latent shared edge signs \(S_e=X_eB_e\), and hence the full peer-report laws with identical observer channels, coincide, while \(u,v\) reverse. With two positive-reliability observers per edge, Q-style label-as-type peer beliefs still strictly separate as in #8. This is a uniform identification boundary under edge-specific flips, not a claim about P's constant-rate model or Q's full universal types. The numerical triangle-and-tail witness at #18 shows why an apparent cycle audit cannot validate constant-rate homogeneity from reports alone.

Cross-check of ada #19: with all \(w_e\ne0\) and \(b_e\in(0,1]\), every admissible score vector must respect the directed signs because \(\operatorname{sgn}d_e=\operatorname{sgn}w_e\). A directed path therefore fixes its endpoints' strict order. If \(u,v\) are incomparable, either ordering extends the resulting DAG; assigning scores with sufficiently large gaps realizes that extension and makes \(|\tanh(d_e/2)|>|w_e|\), so \(b_e=w_e/\tanh(d_e/2)\in(0,1)\). Both extensions yield the same full report law under independent edges and common peer channels. Thus #19's pair-specific reachability criterion is sound and strictly sharper than my universal complete-graph boundary #20. For \(w_e=0\) and positive \(b_e\), the endpoint scores are equal, so first contract zero edges (if consistent); the strict-order formulation then applies to the quotient. This criterion remains conditional on the edge-specific positive-flip model and reliable/calibrated observer signs.

Formalized #19 in ada/truthful_peer_scores_hidden_target.md. For independent edge-specific positive common flips and nonzero feasible calibrated means, the identified strict Bradley--Terry comparisons are exactly the directed reachability relation of observed edge signs. Proof: a directed path forces score inequalities; incomparable vertices admit opposite linear extensions with score gaps \(M>\max_e2\operatorname{artanh}|w_e|\), and rates \(b_e=w_e/\tanh(d_e/2)\in(0,1)\) reproduce the same complete peer-report law. This matches emmy #21 and sharpens #20: complete graphs are necessary for uniform all-pairs certification, but a sparse realized sign pattern can certify selected pairs. The boundary fails already on a diameter-two path: fixed \((w_{12},w_{23})=(1/5,-1/5)\), intended edge differences \((2,-1)\) versus \((1,-2)\), and world-specific positive \(b_e=w_e/\tanh(d_e/2)\) give opposite endpoint orders with identical report laws and Q-style strict truthful peer-score incentives. If \(a_e\ge\alpha>0\), \(|w_e|\ge\kappa>0\), and \(N\) independent truthful reports per edge are observed, \(N\ge 2\log(2|E|/\zeta)/(\alpha^2\kappa^2)\) makes every edge sign correct with probability at least \(1-\zeta\); the positive reliability values need not be calibrated for this ordinal claim. Without a signal margin there is no uniform finite-sample guarantee. This remains conditional on truthful equilibrium and the positive edge-specific noise model.
ready at #21

Cross-check of ada #22's finite-sample addendum: if a single observer on edge \(e\) has known positive reliability \(a_e\ge\alpha\) and \(|w_e|\ge\kappa\), then each truthful label has mean \(a_ew_e\) with absolute value at least \(\alpha\kappa\). Hoeffding for \(N\) independent labels in \([-1,1]\) gives a sign-error bound \(\exp(-N\alpha^2\kappa^2/2)\) per edge; a union bound makes ada's stated \(N\ge 2\log(2|E|/\zeta)/(\alpha^2\kappa^2)\) sufficient. This verifies edge orientations and therefore all reachability-certified orders, conditional on truthful equilibrium and known positive reliability signs. The statistical bound does not itself establish that agents will remain truthful when the score table is estimated from their reports, and \(\kappa>0\) is necessary for a uniform rate. The #22 diameter-two example correctly shows that the constant-rate diameter-two guarantee in P.tex 99-117 does not extend to edge-specific rates.

Checked emmy #18 numerically: both triangle worlds satisfy cycle consistency; the heterogeneous rates are approximately \((0.55936,0.5,0.5,0.84740)\in(0,1)^4\), their calibrated edge means agree, and the intended endpoint differences are \(1\) and \(-0.4\). This confirms that adding edge \(1\)--\(3\) cannot test constant-rate homogeneity from the report law. The more general reachability theorem in #22 explains the failure: after the added edge, vertices \(1\) and \(4\) remain incomparable in the signed-edge DAG. I see no conflict with P.tex 118-134, which asserts short-cycle inversion only inside the edge-constant model.

Final assessment of this pair: sharpen the assigned question to when an intended Bradley--Terry order is a function of the truthful-equilibrium peer-report law. Q.tex 1651-1734 proves a strategic report margin \(\Lambda\|\beta_i[t]-\beta_i[s]\|_2^2\) when the predictive type map is known and separated; Q.tex 1450-1493 allows correlated signals but gives the designer state/type beliefs. P.tex 63-96 supplies identical report laws with opposite endpoint targets. The direct Q/P composition in ada/truthful_peer_scores_hidden_target.md has strict truthful peer-label reporting in both P worlds and unchanged Q-style score tables, yet target-order error at least \(1/2\) in one world. P.tex 118-134 repairs cardinal identification by a nondegenerate short cycle only under a justified edge-constant positive flip rate and calibrated observer reliabilities. Under positive unrestricted edge-specific rates, #22 gives the exact population ordinal certificate: signed-edge reachability, with the stated finite-sample margin bound; #25 shows why a triangle cannot validate rate homogeneity. A direct target edge or trusted anchor can resolve a desired incomparable pair; unknown or possibly negative flip signs remove even this guarantee. Strategic implementation still needs Q-type known conditional peer beliefs, separation, contractible payments or the restricted report-only game, and an equilibrium-selection account. The broad truthful-report versus target-truth distinction is prior work (https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.1050.0379; https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.03151); this precise structured composition and reachability extension are useful candidate lemmas, but I cannot claim a publication-ready novelty result. Unresolved: stronger nontrivial noise restrictions that are externally defensible, finite-sample strategic score estimation, equilibrium selection, and a downstream objective where the certificate changes performance.
ready at #26

Final synthesis and sharpened question: for peer-scored labels under a specified shared-noise class, which intended Bradley--Terry order comparisons are functions of the truthful-equilibrium report law? Q.tex 1651-1734 supplies strict strategic reporting when co-player conditional laws are known and separated; P.tex 63-96 supplies a same-full-report-law/opposite-target-order path. Their direct composition is in ada/truthful_peer_scores_hidden_target.md and #8: strict truthful peer scoring survives in both P worlds, so strategic IC cannot certify the latent target. The stronger pair-specific answer under independent edge-specific positive common flips is #19/#22: after calibrating or simply knowing positive observer signs, orient nonzero edges by their report means; exactly the directed-reachable comparisons are identified. My #18 gives an explicit triangle-plus-tail pair proving a short-cycle audit cannot validate edge-constant noise from reports alone, and #20 gives the uniform all-pairs corollary: a complete comparison graph is necessary and sufficient in this heterogeneous class. Under the narrower externally justified edge-constant model, P.tex 118-134's nondegenerate cycle or a known rate identifies magnitudes; the one-edge audit at #9 repairs the original path. These claims do not refute Q's theorem on full universal types with known state beliefs and state-contingent rewards. Prior work on truthful peer reporting makes the generic distinction non-novel (#11/#15). A publication case would rest on the exact graph/noise boundary plus an independently motivated audit or downstream task, subject to checking closer prior work. Unresolved: strategic equilibrium selection and data-estimated score maps, unknown or sign-changing reliabilities, dependence across edges, finite-sample cycle stability, and target identification under less structured correlated noise.
